chief_complaint: sudden smooth circular bald patch on scalp
hpi_details: A 53-year-old male presents to the clinic with sudden smooth circular bald patch on scalp. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he caught ringworm from his daughter's new kitten or that severe stress from overtime at work made a clump of hair fall out.
concerns: He is worried that the hair loss will spread rapidly until he is completely bald before his son's upcoming wedding.
expectations: He hopes to receive a medicated lotion or a scalp injection today to stimulate the hair follicles to grow back immediately.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Alopecia Areata is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Alopecia Areata: Intralesional Triamcinolone injections monthly, reassure, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Alopecia Areata.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Tinea capitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Rapid progression to total scalp (alopecia totalis) or total body (alopecia universalis) hair loss — indicates worse prognosis and need for specialist referral.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: An autoimmune attack on hair follicles causing a sudden, smooth, circular bald patch on the scalp.
red_flags: Rapid progression to total scalp (alopecia totalis) or total body (alopecia universalis) hair loss — indicates worse prognosis and need for specialist referral
Nail pitting or dystrophy — marker of more severe or active disease
Symptoms of coexisting autoimmune disease (thyroid dysfunction, vitiligo) — screen for associated conditions

must_ask.say: Is the skin underneath smooth, without scaling?
How many patches do you have?
Have you had significant stress recently?

history.answer: I noticed a completely bald, round spot on my head recently, and it looks like it has been slowly spreading.
It started very suddenly about two weeks ago. My wife pointed it out while cutting my hair, and it seemed to appear overnight.
It is located right on top of my scalp near the crown. It has not spread to other parts of my body.
There is just one single circular patch on my head. I have checked the rest of my head and haven't seen any others.
The skin is completely smooth, soft, and bare, almost like the palm of my hand. There is no redness, rash, or crusting.
It started about the size of a coin, but over the past week it has gradually expanded and gotten noticeably wider.
No, I don't feel any urge to pull, twist, or pluck my hair out. The hair just fell out on its own.
No, it does not itch, burn, or hurt at all. My scalp feels completely normal to the touch.
No, there is no dandruff, flaking, or scaling anywhere on that spot or my scalp.
No, my beard, eyebrows, eyelashes, and body hair are all completely normal and full.
No, my fingernails and toenails look normal and smooth. I haven't noticed any pits, ridges, or dents on them.
Yes, I have been feeling unusually tired and run-down lately, though I assumed it was just from working late.
No, I haven't had any sensitivity to heat or cold, heart palpitations, or tremors.
No, I haven't noticed any pale or white patches on my skin, nor any unexplained rashes.
No fever, chills, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss.
I have been under an immense amount of stress at work over the past couple of months due to major company layoffs and restructuring.
No, we do not have pets, and I haven't had contact with farm animals or anyone with a fungal infection.
No, I haven't used any hair dyes, perms, or harsh chemicals. I just wash with my usual gentle shampoo.
No, this is the very first time in my life I've had sudden hair loss or a bald spot.
I applied an over-the-counter scalp tonic my friend suggested for a few days, but it made no difference at all.
It makes me feel very self-conscious around coworkers, so I've been wearing a cap whenever I can.
I thought maybe I caught ringworm from my daughter's new rescue kitten, or that work stress just made a chunk of hair fall out.
I'm terrified this bald spot is going to keep expanding until I lose all my hair right before my son's wedding next month.
I was hoping you could prescribe a lotion or give me an injection in the scalp so the hair starts growing back right away.
I have no chronic medical conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, or autoimmune disorders.
I have never had surgery and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
No, I don't have any known allergies to medications or foods.
My father had typical age-related receding hair, but no one in my family has had circular patchy bald spots or autoimmune conditions.
I work as an office manager and live with my wife. I don't smoke cigarettes, and I only have a beer occasionally on weekends.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-nourished, well-developed male in no acute distress, appearing mildly anxious.

A well-demarcated, smooth, circular 3 cm bald patch on the scalp vertex without erythema, scale, induration, or scarring; exclamation point hairs visible at the margin; fingernails and toenails show no pitting or dystrophy.
No palpable occipital, postauricular, or cervical lymphadenopathy.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, with smooth contours and no palpable nodules or bruit.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are anicteric.
